frontMatter.welcome:
RS Composite believes that its people are the foundation of its success. This Employee Handbook has been developed to provide clear guidance on workplace standards, employment practices, and shared responsibilities that support a safe, respectful, and productive work environment.
The handbook serves as a reference for employees to understand their rights, obligations, and the company’s expectations regarding conduct, performance, health and safety, and ethical behavior. By working together in line with these principles, RS Composite aims to foster trust, transparency, and long-term mutual growth.
The purpose of this Employee Handbook is to:
- Communicate RS Composite’s workplace principles, values, and standards
- Outline employment conditions, policies, and procedures applicable across operations
- Promote fair treatment, dignity, and equal opportunity for all employees
- Support compliance with applicable labour laws, regulations, and international good practices
- Provide employees with guidance on reporting concerns and seeking support
This handbook is designed to ensure consistency in people management practices while encouraging responsible behavior and accountability at all levels.
This Employee Handbook applies to all permanent, temporary, contractual, and probationary employees of RS Composite, regardless of role, designation, or department. Where applicable, certain provisions may also extend to trainees, apprentices, and workers engaged through authorized contractors.
All employees are expected to read, understand, and comply with the provisions outlined in this handbook as a condition of employment.

chapters.title: Conflict of Interest Guidelines
chapters.text:
[table]
| Requirement | Employee Responsibility |
| Disclosure | Promptly report any actual or potential conflict |
| Personal gain | Do not use position or information for personal benefit |
| External activities | Avoid activities that compromise objectivity |
| Decision-making | Act in the best interest of the company |
Failure to disclose conflicts may result in disciplinary action.
## Prevention of Bribery, Corruption, and Fraud
RS Composite maintains a zero-tolerance approach toward bribery, corruption, fraud, and other unethical practices. Employees must not offer, accept, or solicit bribes, kickbacks, or improper benefits in any form.
Gifts or hospitality that could influence business decisions or create a perception of undue influence are prohibited unless explicitly approved by management in line with company guidelines.
## Protection of Company Assets and Information
Employees are responsible for safeguarding company assets, including machinery, equipment, materials, documents, and digital systems. Assets must be used only for authorized work-related purposes.
Confidential information, including business data, employee records, and customer information, must be handled responsibly and protected against unauthorized access, disclosure, or misuse.
## Communication, Transparency, and Truthful Reporting
Employees are expected to communicate honestly and transparently in all work-related matters. Records, reports, and communications must be accurate and complete.
Providing false, misleading, or incomplete information is considered a serious breach of company standards.
## Raising Concerns and Ethical Reporting
RS Composite encourages employees to raise concerns regarding unethical conduct, policy violations, unsafe practices, or any behavior inconsistent with company standards. Concerns may be raised through supervisors, Human Resources, or designated grievance mechanisms.
Employees who report concerns in good faith will be protected from retaliation. Confidentiality will be maintained to the extent possible.
## Corrective and Disciplinary Measures
Violations of workplace conduct and ethical standards may result in corrective or disciplinary action, depending on the nature, severity, and frequency of the violation. Actions may range from counseling and warnings to suspension or termination, in accordance with applicable laws and company procedures.
Disciplinary actions will be applied consistently, fairly, and objectively.
## Leadership Accountability
Managers and supervisors are responsible for:
- Leading by example and modeling ethical behavior
- Communicating workplace standards clearly to their teams
- Monitoring compliance with this handbook
- Addressing concerns and violations promptly and fairly
Effective leadership is critical to maintaining a culture of integrity and accountability.
## Awareness, Training, and Continuous Improvement
RS Composite provides periodic awareness and training programs to ensure employees understand workplace conduct expectations and ethical responsibilities. Feedback from employees, audits, and internal reviews is used to strengthen policies and improve implementation.
## Working Hours and Overtime Management
## Commitment to Responsible and Lawful Working Time
RS Composite recognizes that responsible management of working hours is essential to employee health, safety, wellbeing, and sustainable business performance. The company is committed to organizing work in a manner that prevents excessive fatigue, ensures adequate rest, and supports a healthy work–life balance.
Working hours and overtime are planned, monitored, and reviewed systematically to ensure compliance with applicable labour laws of Bangladesh and to promote fair and humane working conditions.
## Legal and Regulatory Framework
RS Composite conducts its operations in full compliance with the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006, along with subsequent amendments, rules, and notifications issued by the relevant authorities.
The company’s working time practices are aligned with legal provisions governing:
- Maximum daily and weekly working hours
- Mandatory weekly rest days
- Overtime limits and voluntary participation
- Overtime wage rates
- Maintenance of attendance and working hour records
Where internal company practices exceed statutory requirements, the higher standard is applied.
## Normal Working Hours and Weekly Schedule
RS Composite follows a structured working schedule designed to meet production requirements while ensuring legal compliance and employee wellbeing.
## Standard Working Hours Framework
[table]
| Parameter | Applicable Practice at RS Composite |
| Standard working hours per day | 8 hours |
| Standard working days per week | 6 days |
| Total working hours per week | 48 hours |
| Weekly rest day | 1 day per week, as per shift or departmental schedule |

chapters.title: Employee Communication and Awareness
chapters.text:
Employees are informed of their working hours, shift schedules, overtime conditions, and compensation during induction and through ongoing communication. Supervisors play a key role in ensuring that employees understand their rights related to working hours and rest periods.
Information is communicated through:
- Induction programs
- Departmental briefings
- Notice boards and written communications
## Overtime Governance and Compensation for Additional Working Hours
RS Composite manages overtime through structured controls and transparent compensation practices to ensure that additional working hours are fair, lawful, and properly compensated.
Overtime is treated as an exceptional operational requirement and not as a routine expectation. It is undertaken only when necessary to meet urgent production needs, delivery timelines, or unforeseen operational demands. All overtime must receive prior approval from authorized supervisors.
Participation in overtime is strictly voluntary. Employees are not pressured or coerced into working beyond their normal schedules. Total working hours, including overtime, are monitored to ensure compliance with legal limits under the Bangladesh Labour Act.
All additional and atypical working hours are compensated in accordance with applicable law and internal guidelines. Overtime wages are calculated based on verified attendance records and paid at premium rates. Work performed on weekly rest days or public holidays is compensated through enhanced wage rates or compensatory leave, where applicable.
Human Resources conducts monthly reviews of overtime data to identify:
- Departments with frequent overtime
- Repeated overtime for individual employees
- Patterns indicating workload imbalance
Where excessive or recurring overtime is identified, corrective actions such as manpower planning adjustments, shift restructuring, or production rescheduling are implemented. This integrated approach ensures both control of overtime and fair compensation for additional work.
## Overtime and Bonus Guidelines
[table]
| Scheme | Eligibility | Payment Basis |
| Overtime Work | Employees working beyond 8 hours/day | 2× ordinary hourly rate |
| Work on Weekly / Public Holidays | All eligible employees | 2–2.5× daily wage or compensatory leave |
| Performance Bonus | Based on KPIs and appraisal outcomes | Variable, performance-linked |
| Festival / Recognition Bonus | All eligible employees | Fixed or discretionary |
## Wage Adequacy and Wage Review Mechanism
RS Composite recognizes that compliance with minimum wages alone is not sufficient to ensure wage adequacy. The company periodically reviews wage levels to ensure they remain fair and appropriate within the local economic context.
Wage reviews consider:
- Government-notified minimum wages
- Inflation and cost-of-living trends
- Industry wage benchmarks in the garment sector
- Skill level, experience, and job responsibility
- Internal wage parity
Wage adjustments are typically carried out during annual increments or when significant economic changes occur. HR documents wage review outcomes and recommendations for management approval.
## Support for Family and Care Responsibilities
RS Composite implements proactive family-friendly measures to support employees in balancing work and personal responsibilities.
## Maternity and Paternity Leave
- Female employees are entitled to fully paid maternity leave in line with national regulations.
- Male employees may avail paternity leave to support their families during and after childbirth.
- HR guides employees on documentation and ensures smooth processing without loss of benefits.
## Childcare Support
- On-site or nearby childcare facilities are made available to support working parents.
- Facilities are managed by trained caregivers in a safe and hygienic environment.
## Educational Support for Children
- Scholarship support is available for school-going children of employees who demonstrate academic merit.
- Eligibility criteria and timelines are communicated annually by HR.
## Compassionate and Family Emergency Leave
- Employees facing family emergencies may apply for compassionate leave.
- Leave may be extended beyond statutory limits on a case-by-case basis with HR approval.
## Flexible Work Options for Parents
- Employees returning from maternity or paternity leave may request temporary flexible arrangements such as adjusted shifts or partial remote work (where feasible).
## Family-Friendly Benefits Overview
[table]
| Benefit | Eligibility | Duration / Support | Access Process |
| Maternity Leave | Female employees | 16 weeks paid | HR application with medical documents |
| Paternity Leave | Male employees | 10 days paid | HR request with supporting documents |

| Education Scholarships | Employees’ children | Annual | HR application based on merit |

chapters.title: Emergency Preparedness and Incident Response Management
chapters.text:
## Purpose and Regulatory Alignment
RS Composite maintains a structured emergency preparedness and response system to protect employees, contractors, visitors, and property in the event of emergencies. The objective is to minimize injury, loss of life, and operational disruption through clear procedures, trained personnel, and regular preparedness checks.
Emergency preparedness measures are implemented in accordance with the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006, relevant Factory Rules, fire safety regulations, and local authority requirements.
## dentification of Emergency Scenarios
RS Composite identifies potential emergency situations based on operational risks, past incidents, and risk assessment outcomes. Emergency scenarios considered include, but are not limited to:
- Fire and smoke incidents
- Machinery-related accidents and entrapment
- Electrical short circuits and shocks
- Chemical spills, leaks, or fumes
- Explosions or boiler-related incidents
- Slips, falls, or structural emergencies
- Medical emergencies and serious injuries
Each scenario is evaluated to determine response requirements, evacuation needs, and medical intervention measures.
## Emergency Response Plan Structure
RS Composite maintains a documented Emergency Response and Evacuation Plan that is accessible to all employees. The plan clearly defines:
- Emergency reporting procedures
- Roles and responsibilities during emergencies
- Evacuation routes and assembly points
- Communication and alarm systems
- Coordination with external emergency services
Emergency instructions are displayed prominently in operational areas, including production floors, dormitories (where applicable), and common areas.
## Emergency Roles and Responsibilities
Designated personnel are appointed to manage emergencies effectively.
## Emergency Response Roles
[table]
| Role | Key Responsibility |
| Emergency Response Team (ERT) | Overall coordination during emergencies |
| Fire Wardens | Floor-wise evacuation and headcount |
| First Aid Responders | Immediate medical assistance |
| Maintenance Team | Isolation of power, gas, and machinery |
| Security Personnel | Access control and external coordination |
All designated personnel receive role-specific training and refresher sessions.
## Emergency Infrastructure and Equipment
RS Composite ensures availability and maintenance of emergency equipment, including:
- Fire extinguishers and hose reels
- Fire alarms and smoke detectors
- Emergency lighting and exit signage
- First-aid boxes and stretchers
- Spill control kits for chemicals
Equipment locations are clearly marked, and access is kept unobstructed at all times.
## Emergency Drills and Preparedness Testing
Emergency drills are conducted to test preparedness, employee awareness, and response effectiveness.
## Drill Management Practices
- Fire and evacuation drills conducted at least once per year
- Drill participation includes all shifts and departments
- Evacuation time and headcount accuracy are recorded
- Gaps and delays are identified and documented
Post-drill evaluations are carried out to identify improvement actions, which are tracked to closure.
## Communication During Emergencies
Clear communication is critical during emergencies. RS Composite ensures:
- Audible alarms across work areas
- Clear verbal instructions by trained personnel
- Emergency contact numbers displayed prominently
- Communication protocols for informing management and authorities
Employees are trained to follow instructions calmly and avoid panic during emergency situations.
## Medical Emergency and Injury Response
In case of injuries or medical emergencies:
- First aid is provided immediately by trained responders
- On-site medical facilities are activated, where available
- External medical services are contacted when required
- Incident details are recorded for investigation and follow-up
Employees are never penalized for seeking medical assistance.
## Post-Emergency Review and Improvement
After any emergency or drill, RS Composite conducts a structured review to evaluate:
- Response effectiveness
- Equipment performance
- Employee awareness and behavior
- Coordination among response teams
Findings are documented, corrective actions are assigned, and emergency plans are updated accordingly.
## Training and Employee Awareness
All employees receive emergency response training during induction and periodic refresher sessions. Training covers:
- Emergency reporting procedures
- Evacuation routes and assembly points
- Use of basic firefighting equipment (where applicable)
- Personal safety responsibilities
Training attendance and drill participation records are maintained.
## Records and Audit Trail
The following records are maintained:
- Emergency Response Plan documents
- Emergency drill reports and attendance sheets
- Equipment inspection and maintenance logs
- Incident and emergency response reports
These records demonstrate preparedness and compliance during audits and inspections.

chapters.title: Employee Training and Awareness on Ergonomics
chapters.text:
Employees receive ergonomic awareness training as part of:
- Induction training
- Job-specific safety training
- Periodic refresher sessions
Training covers:
- Correct posture and seating position
- Safe lifting and material handling techniques
- Importance of rest breaks and task variation
- Early signs and symptoms of musculoskeletal strain
Supervisors reinforce ergonomic practices through daily monitoring and coaching.
## Early Reporting and Medical Intervention
Employees are encouraged to report:
- Persistent pain or discomfort
- Numbness, stiffness, or reduced mobility
- Fatigue related to repetitive tasks
Early reporting enables timely medical evaluation and intervention. Where required, temporary job modification, task reassignment, or medical referral is arranged to prevent worsening of the condition.
## ntegration with Health Surveillance
Ergonomic risk management is closely linked with employee health surveillance. Health check-up findings related to musculoskeletal issues are reviewed to:
- Identify high-risk tasks or departments
- Improve ergonomic controls
- Update risk assessments and work design
This integration ensures continuous improvement and prevention of long-term injuries.
## Monitoring, Review, and Continuous Improvement
Ergonomic controls are reviewed through:
- Periodic workstation assessments
- Analysis of health complaints and absenteeism
- Feedback from employees and supervisors
Corrective actions are updated as tasks, layouts, or production methods change.
## Records and Documentation
RS Composite maintains:
- Ergonomic assessment records
- Corrective action logs
- Training attendance records
- Medical referral and follow-up documentation
These records provide traceability and evidence of effective ergonomic risk management.
## Psychological Wellbeing and Workplace Stress Management
## Purpose and Legal Context
RS Composite recognizes that employee health extends beyond physical safety and includes psychological wellbeing and mental health. The company is committed to creating a work environment that minimizes excessive stress, supports emotional wellbeing, and promotes respectful and supportive working relationships.
Measures addressing psychological wellbeing are implemented in alignment with the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006, which requires employers to ensure humane working conditions, reasonable working hours, rest, and protection of employee dignity at work.
## dentification of Psychosocial Risk Factors
RS Composite proactively identifies factors that may contribute to workplace stress or psychological strain through:
- Review of working hours and overtime data
- Employee feedback and satisfaction surveys
- Absenteeism and turnover trends
- Incident and grievance records
- Supervisor observations and discussions
Common psychosocial risk factors assessed include:
- Excessive workload or prolonged overtime
- High work pace or unrealistic production targets
- Role ambiguity or lack of clarity in responsibilities
- Interpersonal conflicts or inappropriate behavior
- Limited rest or recovery time
These risks are reviewed as part of overall workplace risk management.
## Preventive Measures to Reduce Workplace Stress
RS Composite prioritizes preventive actions to reduce stress at its source rather than reacting only after issues arise.
Preventive measures include:
- Workload planning aligned with realistic production capacity
- Enforcement of working hour and rest day requirements
- Clear job roles and performance expectations
- Supervisor training on respectful leadership and communication
- Promotion of a culture where employees can raise concerns openly
Supervisors are responsible for monitoring signs of stress within their teams and addressing issues early.
## Employee Support and Intervention Mechanisms
When employees experience stress or psychological distress, RS Composite provides access to supportive mechanisms.
Support measures include:
- Open-door access to Human Resources for confidential discussions
- Supervisor guidance and referral to HR where concerns are identified
- Temporary job adjustments or workload modification where appropriate
- Referral to medical or counseling services when required
Employees are encouraged to seek support early, and all discussions related to mental wellbeing are handled with confidentiality and sensitivity.
## Respectful Workplace and Dignity at Work
RS Composite maintains a zero-tolerance approach toward harassment, intimidation, or abusive behavior. Respectful behavior is reinforced through:
- Workplace conduct guidelines
- Awareness training on acceptable behavior
- Clear reporting and grievance mechanisms
A respectful workplace significantly reduces psychological stress and contributes to overall wellbeing.
## Monitoring and Review of Psychological Wellbeing
Psychological wellbeing measures are reviewed through:
- Analysis of employee feedback and survey results
- Monitoring of absenteeism and overtime patterns

chapters.title: Performance Evaluation and Ongoing Individual Assessment
chapters.text:
## Purpose and Management Commitment
RS Composite implements a structured and consistent performance evaluation process to assess individual employee performance on a regular basis. The purpose of this process is to provide constructive feedback, identify strengths and improvement areas, support employee development, and recognize high performers.
Performance assessment is treated as a management tool for continuous improvement, not merely as an administrative exercise. The process is applied fairly across roles and functions and aligns with principles of transparency, objectivity, and non-discrimination.
## Scope of Performance Assessment
Performance evaluations apply to:
- Permanent and contractual employees
- Production, maintenance, supervisory, and administrative roles
- New employees after completion of probation
- Existing employees on a defined review cycle
Assessment criteria are adapted to the nature of each role while maintaining consistency in evaluation standards.
## Performance Assessment Criteria
RS Composite uses a combination of quantitative and qualitative indicators to ensure a balanced and role-relevant evaluation.
## Key Performance Dimensions
- Productivity and output quality
- Compliance with safety and operational procedures
- Attendance, punctuality, and discipline
- Job knowledge and technical competence
- Teamwork, communication, and initiative
This approach ensures that performance is not judged solely on output, but also on behavior, compliance, and contribution to team effectiveness.
## Performance Review Cycle and Frequency
Performance assessments are conducted at defined intervals to ensure regular feedback and timely intervention.
## Performance Review Framework
[table]
| Review Type | Applicable Employees | Frequency | Conducted By | Purpose |
| Probation Review | New employees | End of probation period | Supervisor & HR | Confirm role suitability and training needs |
| Annual Performance Review | All employees | Once per year | Immediate Supervisor | Evaluate overall performance and development |
| Interim Review | Employees with role change or performance gaps | As required | Supervisor | Monitor progress and provide support |
| Promotion Readiness Review | Promotion candidates | As applicable | Supervisor & Management | Assess readiness for higher responsibility |
This structured cycle ensures that performance is reviewed consistently and not on an ad-hoc basis.
## Performance Review Process
The evaluation process follows defined steps:
- Supervisor reviews attendance, productivity, quality, and safety records
- Qualitative assessment is made based on observation and interaction
- Performance strengths and improvement areas are documented
- Feedback discussion is conducted with the employee
- Development actions or corrective measures are agreed
- Review outcomes are formally recorded and acknowledged
Employees are encouraged to actively participate in review discussions and share their perspectives.
## Use of Performance Assessment Outcomes
Performance evaluation outcomes are actively used to:
- Identify individual training and upskilling needs
- Support decisions on promotions or internal mobility
- Recognize consistent high performance
- Address performance gaps through coaching or training
- Inform incentive or reward decisions, where applicable
This ensures the process leads to practical development outcomes, not just documentation.
## Fairness, Objectivity, and Non-Discrimination
To maintain fairness:
- Supervisors are guided on objective evaluation methods
- Criteria are job-related and applied consistently
- Discriminatory factors are strictly excluded
- HR reviews appraisal records for consistency
Employees may raise concerns regarding assessments, which are reviewed by HR to ensure fairness.
## Documentation and Recordkeeping
RS Composite maintains:
- Completed performance appraisal forms
- Supervisor assessment notes
- Employee feedback acknowledgments
- Agreed development or improvement plans
These records are retained securely and reviewed during audits or management reviews.
## Continuous Improvement of the Performance System
The performance evaluation framework is reviewed periodically to:
- Improve clarity of evaluation criteria
- Strengthen consistency across departments
- Incorporate employee and supervisor feedback
## ndividual Development and Career Planning Framework
## Purpose and Strategic Intent
RS Composite is committed to supporting the long-term professional growth of its employees by providing a structured and transparent Individual Development and Career Planning (IDP) framework. This framework enables employees to grow according to their skills, potential, and career aspirations while ensuring alignment with organizational needs.
The objective of this process is to move beyond short-term performance management and actively support sustainable careers, internal talent development, and employee retention.

chapters.title: Gender Equality and Prevention of Sexual Harassment at the Workplace
chapters.text:
## Commitment to Gender Equity and Safe Work Environment
RS Composite is committed to fostering a workplace that promotes gender equality, dignity, and safety for all employees. The company strictly prohibits sexual harassment in any form and actively works to ensure that all individuals—regardless of gender—can work in an environment free from intimidation, discrimination, or abuse.
These measures are aligned with the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006, relevant rules and notifications, and the High Court Guidelines on Sexual Harassment Prevention (2009), which require employers to take proactive steps to prevent and address sexual harassment at the workplace.
## Scope and Applicability
This framework applies to:
- All employees, including permanent, temporary, probationary, and contract workers
- Supervisors, managers, and senior leadership
- Third parties, vendors, visitors, and service providers interacting with employees
- All work-related locations, including production areas, offices, training spaces, and company-provided facilities
The protections apply during working hours, breaks, overtime, training, and work-related travel or events.
## Definition and Forms of Sexual Harassment
RS Composite recognizes sexual harassment as any unwelcome behavior of a sexual nature that creates an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment.
Examples include, but are not limited to:
- Unwelcome physical contact or advances
- Sexually suggestive comments, jokes, or gestures
- Requests for sexual favors, whether explicit or implied
- Display or sharing of inappropriate images or messages
- Staring, leering, or intrusive behavior
- Retaliation linked to rejection of sexual advances
Such conduct is strictly prohibited irrespective of intent, seniority, or gender of the parties involved.
## Preventive Measures and Gender-Sensitive Workplace Practices
RS Composite implements proactive measures to prevent sexual harassment and promote gender equality, including:
- Clear written policies communicated to all employees
- Gender-sensitive induction and refresher training
- Supervisor accountability for respectful conduct
- Separate and secure sanitation facilities where required
- Adequate lighting and safety measures in work areas
- Encouragement of respectful communication and behavior
These measures aim to reduce risk factors and foster a culture of mutual respect.
## nternal Complaints Committee (ICC) / Complaint Handling Mechanism
In line with national requirements, RS Composite has established a confidential and accessible complaint-handling mechanism to address sexual harassment cases.
Key features include:
- Designated trained members to receive complaints
- Confidential handling of all complaints
- Fair, impartial, and timely investigation
- Opportunity for both parties to be heard
- Protection of complainants from retaliation
Employees may raise complaints verbally or in writing and may seek support during the process.
## Reporting Channels and Employee Support
Employees may report sexual harassment through:
- Designated complaint committee members
- Human Resources
- Confidential grievance mechanisms
Support is provided to complainants, including guidance on the process, assurance of confidentiality, and protection against victimization.
## nvestigation, Disciplinary Action, and Remediation
All complaints are:
- Investigated promptly and objectively
- Reviewed in accordance with internal procedures and legal requirements
- Addressed through proportionate disciplinary measures
Disciplinary actions may include:
- Counseling or formal warnings
- Suspension or termination
- Other corrective actions as appropriate
Where necessary, corrective measures are also taken to prevent recurrence.
## Training, Awareness, and Communication
Awareness on gender equality and sexual harassment prevention is reinforced through:
- Mandatory induction training
- Periodic refresher sessions
- Supervisor and leadership briefings
- Display of policy information and reporting channels
Training emphasizes respect, consent, appropriate conduct, and available support systems.
## Monitoring, Review, and Continuous Improvement
RS Composite monitors the effectiveness of its gender equality and harassment prevention measures through:
- Review of complaint data and trends
- Employee feedback mechanisms
- Internal audits and management reviews
Findings are used to strengthen policies, training content, and preventive controls.
## Documentation and Audit Readiness
The company maintains:
- Gender equality and anti-sexual harassment policies
- Training attendance and materials
- Complaint and investigation records
- Corrective and disciplinary action documentation
